{{1955 Midwest Conference football standings}}
The '''1955 Coe Kohawks football team''' represented [[Coe College]] as a member of the [[Midwest Conference]] (MWC) during the [[1955 college football season]]. Led by [[Dick Clausen]] in his eighth and final season as head coach, the Kohawks compiled a perfect overall record of 8–0 with a mark of 7–0 in conference play, winning the MWC title.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Cornell Has Best Record Since 1947 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette/141779160/ |newspaper=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Cedar Rapids Gazette]] |location=[[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]] |date=November 13, 1955 |page=1, section 5 |access-date=February 21, 2024 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{Open access}} }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Conference Football Standings 1955 |url=https://static.midwestconference.org/custompages/Past%20MWC%20Seasons/Football/1954-57%20fb%20standings.pdf |publisher=[[Midwest Conference]] |access-date=February 21, 2024 }}</ref>

After the season, Coe received a "feeler" from representatives of the [[Citrus Bowl|Tangerine Bowl]]. To play in a [[bowl game]], Coe needed approval from the other MWC schools. The matter was put to a vote, and the MWC schools voted 6–3 against allowing the Kohawks to play in the bowl.<ref>{{cite news|title=Vote Against Coe Play in Bowl Game|newspaper=The Cedar Rapids Gazette|date=November 19, 1955|page=3|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette-vote-against-coe-play-in-bow/141825354/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Quarterback Elliott "Shady" Day was selected as the team's most valuable player.<ref>{{cite news|title=Coe Honors Day, Phillips|newspaper=The Cedar Rapids Gazette|date=December 3, 1955|page=5|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette-coe-honors-day-phillips/141826634/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> Day completed 38 of 71 passes for 712 yards.<ref name=Shade/> End George Cilek was selected as a second-team player on the [[1955 Little All-America college football team]]. Day received honorable mention.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cilek, Schultz Are Honored|newspaper=The Cedar Rapids Gazette|date=December 1, 1955|page=45|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette-cilek-schultz-are-honored/141825799/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> John "Crunch" Rosenberg ranked fourth in the nation in scoring among small college players.<ref name=Shade>{{cite news|title=Shades of Championship|newspaper=The Coe Cosmos|date=December 15, 1955|page=3|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-coe-cosmos-shades-of-championship/141826347/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

Coe played home games at [[Kingston Stadium]] in [[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]].
